# Fusion-law plateau on the degree-150 triple (49,12,116)

Using the same certificate teacher and the same cyclic sidecar construction, the moduli

`2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13`

all give the same held-rank vector `(2,1,3,250)` and MRR `0.4593333333333333`. At modulus 16 the vector changes to `(2,1,5,250)`, MRR `0.426`.

This plateau is not caused by identical sidecar feature spaces. After residualizing out everything linearly predictable from the fixed 152-dimensional Wilson packet, the cyclic sidecar residual ranks are 18 for C4, 30 for C8 and 42 for C16. The C4/C8 residual subspaces are highly aligned (mean canonical correlation about 0.989), but C8 contains genuinely additional directions. Those extra directions do not improve the held transport; at C16 the extra capacity begins to hurt Q58.

The current bottleneck is therefore not simply the number of central frequencies. The persistent Q107 failure points back to star-graded relation-representation information absent from the present student architecture.
